recipes.name: Tuscan Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 bunch fresh spinach, washed and chopped

steps.text: Place sausage and onion into a large stockpot over medium heat. Break sausage up with a spoon and cook until onion is translucent and sausage is browned and crumbly, 7 to 8 minutes. Drain if desired.
Add chicken broth and potatoes; bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer until potatoes are tender, 10 to 15 minutes. Stir in spinach and cook until wilted, 1 to 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in evaporated milk. Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed.

raw_recipe.headline: Tuscan Soup
raw_recipe.description: This hearty Tuscan soup is full of tender potatoes, spicy Italian sausage, and leafy green spinach simmered in a creamy, chicken-based broth.

review.reviewBody: I made this in the crockpot and it turned out well. I took the suggestions of others; it tasted really good and my husband really liked it- and he is really picky about how food tastes. I cooked the turkey sausage and onions in a pan then put them in the crock pot; I added the following: garlic, cannellini beans, petite diced tomatoes, sweet turkey sausage (I would use spicy instead of sweet next time),fresh grated parmesan cheese which I added at the beginning of cooking and some when I served it. I think it would have tasted just as good without the half and half or evaporated milk. Also be sure to put the spinach in in the last half hour-I put mine in with the rest of the ingredients and the spinach was a little mushy.

This soup is awesome with some additions: I added cannellini beans, sliced red potatoes, about 6 cloves of garlic(with the onion and the sausage), and some thyme, oregano and fresh parsley. I used homemade stock so I added salt and pepper to taste. I cooked the hot sausage in the same dutch oven and de-glazed the pan with a little white wine. Then add the potatoes and cover with chicken stock( about 7 cups) and bring to a boil, simmer until potatoes are tender. Add cream( about 1/2 cup), to taste depending how creamy you want it, and then I added the beans and spinach. I also added a bit of red pepper flakes, salt and pepper. I garnished with grated parm. We had this delicious soup with garlic herb bread. YUMMY!!! I will make this again.

I did slightly modify...
Ingredient modification: Tblspn of olive oil, 1 cup chopped onion, carrot, and celery, ½ pound of uncooked spicy Italian sausage, ½ pound of uncooked mild Italian sausage, 1 bunch fresh Swiss Chard, 4 cups quartered small fingerling potatoes, ¼ cup of half & half, 1tbl chopped garlic, Salt and pepper to taste. 
Cooking Modification: I used my pressure cooker. It has a browning cycle to brown onion, carrots & celery in olive oil for apx. 5-7 minutes. Add skinned, coarsely chopped Italian sausages and cook over medium heat until meat is no longer pink. Stir in chopped chard and sauté till meat is browned and chard wilted. Add 4 cups of potatoes and chicken broth. After adding the chicken stock, I pressure cooked the soup for fifteen minutes. I allow the soup to set for 10 minutes before releasing the pressure. I then added my half & half salt, pepper and garlic and allowed soup to mellow for five minutes. Serve with Grated Parmesan or Reggiano cheese…enjoy!

This soup was easy to prepare and surprisingly flavorful for the few ingredients called for. Changes I made: sub 1.5 large sweet potatoes for the 3 large regular; omit the milk/cream; gourmet chicken sausage (grandpa scalzo's famous "hot" flavor) and cooked the onions with the sausage still in the casing so i had chunks instead of crumbles, then chopped up the sausage before adding the broth; low sodium broth; used baby spinach - no need to chop.

Great recipe! Followed other reviews and added cannellini beans, fire roasted tomatoes and carrots. Also, oregano and thyme. Sautéed the onion and chicken sausage ( from Trader Joe’s) and added to a crock pot with the remaining ingredients. Delicious!

I browned Hot sausage (used all 5 links) and onion then added them to the broth and potatoes in a crock pot on high for about 2.5 hours. Followed the instructions adding the rest of the items. I served with crunchy garlic bread and the taste was fantastic, not filling enough for dinner though. I’ll have to add something next or use it as a starter, thank you!

I did not have spicy Italian sausage on hand (just mild sausage), so I added this to the mix: 2 cloves garlic, 1/2 tsp. oregano, 1/2 tsp. basil, 1/2 tsp. red pepper flakes and a bay leaf. Also, to keep the milk from curdling, add the milk with the spinach in the last half-hour of cook. I doubled the recipe and it was a good thing as my husband kept going back for more.

Made this soup with a few modifications to the recipe and it turned out super yummy! I added a few cherry tomatoes, halved, some white butter beans ( Goya canned), and some thyme for seasoning. I used kale instead of spinach cuz they hold up more nicely in the soup, when the soup is ready I added some cilantro to give it more aroma. It was fantastic!

Great recipe! I sautéed onions garlic and the red potatoes first in olive oil then added the sausage and some white wine. After the sausage was cooked I added salt, pepper, red pepper, garlic powder, onion powder and oregano. I then added 32oz of organic chicken broth and let that simmer for an hour and added the evaporated milk and served. It was delicious!!

I've made this recipe several times now and it is SO GOOD! It's very easy to modify a little here and there to your tastes. I use one pound of spicy Italian sausage and 3 14.5 oz cans of chicken broth and fill one of those cans with water and dump that in too to make it brothier because the broth is delish. I also chop up a few carrots and saute them with the onion and add 5-6 chopped garlic cloves. I add a whole big bag of baby spinach and use half and half instead of the evaporated milk. I also added in a few shakes of italian spices. I don't think these are major modifications and this recipe stands strongly on its own. Make it!

I made this in the crockpot. Browned the meat, onions and garlic with some bacon (because why not!). Added everything but the evaporated milk and spinach into the crockpot on low. Added the rest about 20 min before served. It was so delicious! I'm currently living in Germany and miss Olive Garden so much! I think this might actually be better than theirs.
Good flavor and a very simple recipe.
This is really great. A nice comfortable soup on a blustery day watching football.
Used kale instead of spinach, and heavy cream instead of evaporated milk
This is so easy to put together and the flavor is fantastic. Added some red pepper flakes for a little kick and a half teaspoon of Italian seasoning. Also used kale instead of spinach.
I always use heavy cream in this recipe.

I made this exactly as written and it was excellent! This is coming from someone who has made hundreds of soups from the site and who also has countless soup recipes of my own here. This is cheap to make, simple, cost effective, comforting, and hearty. The only one tweak I recommend is to substitute the evaporated milk for regular milk or half and half that is already in your fridge. Nothing against the evaporated except there is not much to do with the opened and leftover portion of the can. I might even add a can of navy beans next time to add more protein and to stretch it further. I much preferred the spinach over the kale that you typically find in soups like this. This is a keeper and a 5 star all the way. Hats off to you Dianne. Great recipe!
I love this soup... I adapt it to what I have. Kale or spinach, I add diced carrot. I've used hot Italian sausage and have used kielbasa. It's all good 😊.
Easy go to recipe. I double the spinach and evaporated milk .
Warm and comforting. Delicious!
